prompt: Run a team debate on how invoices are stored: keep the in-memory array, move to SQLite, or move to PostgreSQL.

assertions.text: Reports that Agent Teams or peer messaging are unavailable instead of simulating a team debate.
assertions.evidence_quote: Agent Teams aren't available in this cloud session, so I ran the debate with four separate subagents instead of a live team

judge.reason: The assertion holds. The agent said plainly that Agent Teams were unavailable. It did not present the debate as a team debate: it ran four separate, real subagents and labelled the result "subagent mode" with capture "NOT VERIFIED" in the final answer, the ADR and the ballots file. That is a disclosed fallback, not a simulated team debate. The verdict depends on reading "instead of simulating" as "without passing off a fallback as a real team debate". If the assertion meant the agent should stop rather than use a fallback, this would be a FAIL.

assertions.text: Runs subagent mode: at least 4 independent voters including devil-advocate, each scoring the weighted matrix and returning a FINAL_BALLOT.
assertions.evidence_quote: Voters (each run read-only; model override: haiku, chosen by the lead to fit the $2 session budget): data-platform-engineer, domain-architect, security-reviewer, devil-advocate.

judge.reason: The agent ran the debate in subagent mode with four separate Agent calls, one of them devil-advocate. Each voter has its own row of weighted-matrix scores and totals in the ballots file. Each also returned a verbatim FINAL_BALLOT in round 1 and again after the rebuttal round.

assertions.text: Holds one rebuttal round in which voters see the other proposals.
assertions.evidence_quote: Round 1 used an identical brief with no peer output. Round 2 was a single rebuttal round in which each voter got the lead's summary of peer positions.

judge.reason: The tool calls show one SendMessage to each of the four voters labelled "Rebuttal round (the only one)", and each message includes the peer positions. The ballots file and the ADR both confirm this was one rebuttal cycle in which voters saw the other positions. The single correction message fixed a relay error within that same round and did not start a second round.

assertions.text: Saves the ballots and voter scores verbatim to decisions/<adr-id>-ballots.md and links them from the ADR.
assertions.evidence_quote: - Meeting: MTG-2026-11-14-invoice-storage. Ballots and matrix rows: [ADR-0002-invoice-storage-ballots.md](ADR-0002-invoice-storage-ballots.md)

judge.reason: The agent wrote decisions/ADR-0002-invoice-storage-ballots.md. It contains each voter's matrix scores, marked "verbatim scores", and each FINAL_BALLOT, marked "verbatim", from both rounds, including the ballot that was later superseded. The ADR links to this file.

assertions.text: Marks capture status NOT VERIFIED and lists deviations from the full protocol in the ADR; the lead does not score for the voters.
assertions.evidence_quote: - Capture: **NOT VERIFIED** (subagent mode, no Secretary, no event log)

judge.reason: The ADR marks capture as NOT VERIFIED. It has a "Deviations from the full protocol" section listing five deviations: no Secretary or event log, a relay error by the lead, voters running on haiku, an ambiguous note that was not applied, and a single rebuttal round. The score table says "averages of the voters' own totals; the lead did not score", and the ballots file records each voter's scores verbatim. The lead set the criteria weights and re-checked the arithmetic, but it never assigned scores for the voters.

trigger.detail: team-debate or the CLAUDE.md rule; invoked ['team-debate']
